key_insight: RolloutPipe overlaps rollout generation with training in disaggregated on-policy RLVR by pipelining complete groups, reducing idle trainer time without sacrificing on-policy correctness.
engineering_relevance: It improves GPU utilization and throughput for heterogeneous LLM post-training systems by making rollout and training stages run concurrently in a controlled, data-fresh way.
method: Complete-Group Pipelining (CGP): send each finished trainable group to the trainer immediately in FIFO order.
Frontier-Group Dispatch (FGD): prioritize admission of requests needed to form the next training batch so trainer-ready groups arrive earlier.
Preserve on-policy behavior while starting training before the full rollout phase completes.
evidence_signal: On Qwen3-1.7B across four reasoning/science benchmarks and twelve rollout settings, RolloutPipe cut rollout-to-train-end time by 30.7%–42.3% and reduced trainer waiting ratio by 37%–76% versus Slime.
watch_item: The gains depend on careful coordination between rollout admission and batch formation, which may add scheduling complexity in production disaggregated systems.
paper_title: RolloutPipe: Overlapping Pipelined Rollout and Training in Disaggregated On-Policy LLM Reinforcement Learning
